geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the flat generic block into a section-authored hall so the roof can express span/daylight instead of remaining box-like.
Use a shed section as a stable gym-friendly balanced variation and to create directional daylight logic.
Align the span along the long direction so the hall reads as a usable long-span volume.
Wrap the hall with a carved public court while keeping the hall in the ancestry of the new root.
Bound the carve so it reads as a threshold court rather than a detached void.
Open the public court toward the access side specified by the program frame so the frontage becomes legible.
Make the carved court the new root so the access threshold becomes the organizing gesture while preserving the hall as ancestry.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the generic puncture-only massing with a section-aware hall controller so the dominant body can support gym-specific roof/span logic.
Keep the long axis aligned to preserve a hall-like bar rather than turning into a square object.
Reduce puncture repetition so the mass remains one dominant hall volume instead of reading as an abstract perforated block.
Subdue the void impact of puncture; the main fix needed is a carved access threshold and roof section, not more through-holes.
Add a public void to create a legible ground response and entry court on the access side.
Keep the void bounded and architectural rather than consuming the whole mass.

rationale: The candidate reads consistently across the four views as one compact, low rectangular mass, so it is not fragmented and the geometric repair is clean. However, for a gymnasium it remains too generic and too sealed: the dominant body does not clearly read as a long-span hall, the roof/section is flat and unexpressive, and there is no meaningful public void, entry seam, or undercut responding to the verified access edge. The blue frontage line is acknowledged only by a weak side adjacency, not by a legible threshold or public ground figure. As a result, the form is coherent massing but fails the program contract because it does not visibly support clear-span sports space, service hierarchy, or roof/daylight logic.
